clue.text: Take a mushroom into court

indicators.note: into says the mushroom goes inside the abbreviation for court

parts.note: a cep is an edible wild mushroom, the porcini

explanation.surface: Someone carries a mushroom into a courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept an offer is to take it.

clue.text: A heel holds weapon — he spreads panic

indicators.note: holds means the weapon is gripped inside the word for heel

parts.note: a ship that heels leans over, or lists
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: A scoundrel with a gun is terrifying people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heel' looks like a cad or the back of a foot; here it is the nautical verb for leaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who raises needless fears and warnings causes others to feel frightened.

clue.text: Last worker to get fruit pie

explanation.surface: A tradesman fetches a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: A last is the foot-shaped block on which shoes are made or mended, so it is not the opposite of first here.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoemender works on a last; a deep fruit dish topped with scone dough has the same name.

clue.text: Picture shaft of light entering doorway

indicators.note: entering means the shaft of light goes inside the doorway

parts.note: a portal is a grand doorway or gate
a ray is a narrow beam of light

explanation.surface: An image of sunlight streaming through a door.
explanation.definitionFit: A depiction or picture of something is a representation of it.

clue.text: Pretended to have been moved

explanation.surface: Someone faked being touched by emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Affected manners are put on or feigned; to be affected by a story is to be emotionally touched by it.

clue.text: Reckon a talented agent needs optimism

parts.note: to feel that something is so is to reckon it
good means skilled or talented
a factor is an agent who acts for another, such as a land agent

explanation.surface: A gifted representative must have a positive outlook, someone thinks.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a general sense of wellbeing and confidence in a population or economy.

clue.text: Praise previous partner to get money

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
L stands for pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone compliments a former spouse in order to get cash.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud is to praise highly.

clue.text: Manoeuvres with discretion and science back-up

parts.note: tact is discretion in dealing with others

indicators.note: in a down entry, back-up means the letters read upwards, so in reverse

explanation.surface: Military operations need delicacy and technical support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-up' looks like support but, in a down entry, it turns SCI into ICS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactics are the planned moves or schemes used to achieve an aim.

clue.text: Plan to publish study about retired servicemen

annotationWithheld.why: Plan to publish study about retired servicemen (6): DEN around SIG (GIS reversed) gives DESIGN, defined by 'Plan', but 'to publish' has no job in any parse found, so the clue as held looks corrupted
annotationWithheld.clue: Plan to publish study about retired servicemen

clue.text: Frenchman is apt to embezzle funds

parts.note: M stands for Monsieur, the French title for a man
apt means suitable or fitting

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is likely to steal money.
explanation.definitionFit: To take money dishonestly for one's own use is to embezzle it.

clue.text: French inn stocking popular vegetable

indicators.note: stocking means holding something inside, as a shop stocks goods

parts.note: auberge is the French word for an inn
in means fashionable or popular, as in the in crowd

explanation.surface: A country inn in France keeps a well-liked vegetable in stock.
explanation.definitionFit: The eggplant, a purple vegetable, goes by this name in Britain and France.

clue.text: Parasites get credit for correct answers

explanation.surface: Bloodsuckers somehow win marks in a quiz.
explanation.definitionFit: Small bloodsucking arachnids that cling to dogs share their name with the check marks a teacher writes beside right answers.

clue.text: Complaint follows many a Latin song

parts.note: M is a thousand in Roman numerals, standing for many
an aria is a solo song in an opera

explanation.surface: An illness sets in after someone sings lots of Latin airs.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is an illness, and this is a mosquito-borne fever.

clue.text: I'll go back into band, however humiliating

indicators.note: into puts the turned contraction inside the word for a band

parts.note: a gang is a band of people

indicators.note: go back tells us the letters of the contraction run in the opposite direction

parts.note: the contraction written without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone vows to rejoin their group even if it proves embarrassing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something galling is mortifying or bitterly annoying, wounding one's pride.

clue.text: Sprinkle water on a posy

explanation.surface: Someone mists a little bunch of flowers to keep it fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: To spritz is to send fine droplets over something; a small bunch of cut flowers is also called by this name.

clue.text: Priest confronting fiendish female makes headway

parts.note: an ogress is a female ogre, a monstrous creature

explanation.surface: A clergyman faces down a she-devil and comes out ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confronting' only places the priest first; 'makes' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Headway is forward movement, advancement towards a goal.

clue.text: Dress mum for part? What a performance!

parts.note: to rig someone out is to dress them
ma is an informal word for mother
a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: A mother is costumed for a stage part amid great fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What a performance!' is a British exclamation at a tiresome fuss, not praise for acting.
explanation.definitionFit: A tedious, long-winded procedure is a palaver or rigmarole, exactly what the exasperated exclamation complains of.

clue.text: I got badly treated — ditto

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of treated are put in a poor order

explanation.surface: Someone complains of poor treatment, and says it again.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditto something is to repeat it, saying the same again.

clue.text: Strapped for cash? That's quite wrong!

explanation.surface: Short of money, someone is told their guess is way out.
explanation.definitionFit: Being poor means having little money; a guess far from correct is said to be way off the mark.

clue.text: Instrument for a large prickle

parts.note: a thorn is a sharp prickle on a plant

explanation.surface: A tool for removing a big splinter.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a brass musical instrument of the saxhorn family.

clue.text: To transplant tissue is hard work

explanation.surface: Surgery to move skin from one place to another is demanding labour.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons splice tissue or skin onto another site; British slang also uses the word for strenuous toil.

clue.text: Hence us agents in Alabama are not for the party!

indicators.note: in says the two pieces sit inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: AL is the postal abbreviation for Alabama
so means therefore or hence
the CIA is the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: American spies in Alabama refuse to join the celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' suggests politics, but it means a social gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unsociable avoids company and gatherings.

clue.text: A Yemeni leader in squalid house wants sanctuary

indicators.note: in puts the leading letter inside the word for a squalid house

parts.note: a slum is a squalid, rundown dwelling

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word Yemeni

explanation.surface: A man from Yemen, living in poverty, seeks refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: Political asylum is protection or refuge granted by a state.

clue.text: Likely to arrange a trade show

parts.note: to set things is to arrange or place them
a fair is an exhibition of goods, as in a trade fair

explanation.surface: Someone is probably going to organise an exhibition for merchants.
explanation.walkthrough: Set fair is a British weather forecaster's phrase for settled conditions, extended to anything in a good position to succeed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set fair is well placed and probable to go well.

clue.text: States that are endlessly hostile

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: averse means opposed or hostile to something

explanation.surface: Countries that are constantly at war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'States' looks like countries but is the verb: avers means asserts.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to assert or declare firmly.

clue.text: Outcry about many an illicit affair

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
L is fifty in Roman numerals, standing for many
an amour is a love affair, often a secret one

explanation.surface: Public uproar breaks out over a string of scandalous liaisons.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcry is a loud public protest or uproar.

clue.text: Free portion of vindaloo served before 7PM

annotationWithheld.why: Free portion of vindaloo served before 7PM (5): LOOSE is hidden in 'vindaLOO SErved', but 'before 7PM' has no job in any parse found, so the clue as held looks corrupted
annotationWithheld.clue: Free portion of vindaloo served before 7PM

clue.text: Champion awarded vital points after a game

indicators.note: after places the essential points behind the article and the game

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
the gist is the essential points of a matter

explanation.surface: A winner receives crucial points following a match.
explanation.definitionFit: To champion a cause is to defend it, which is what a defender of a belief does.

clue.text: Leading MP is taken in by moneymaker

indicators.note: taken in by means the small word sits inside the word for a moneymaker

parts.note: a minter is one who mints coins, literally making money

explanation.surface: A prominent politician is fooled by a rich businessman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' looks like 'deceived', but it means placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior member of parliament who heads a government department holds this title.

clue.text: The man had eaten fish and bent over

indicators.note: eaten means the fish goes inside, swallowed by the contraction

parts.note: he had shortens to he'd, written without its apostrophe
an eel is a long snakelike fish

explanation.surface: A man ate some fish and then doubled up.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that heels leans over to one side, so it has tilted.
